# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile findings yet. I will ask the Mute for the manual’s rule and for a relay of the Deaf’s visual observations. I will also use a legal gesture to signal the Deaf to communicate those observations through the Mute.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and tell me the exact safe action rule. Ask Deaf to report every visible display, light, colour, marking, and wire detail to you, then relay it to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The display reads 0. The light is red. Wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, and wire 3 is red. I saw Mute gesture thumbs-up twice, thumbs-down twice, OK then crossed fingers; Blind gestured pointing at you.

The Deaf has relayed the bomb’s visible state: display 0, red light, and wire colours blue, green, red. I still do not know the manual’s rule, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. I am asking the Mute to provide the rule and to clarify the coded gestures already observed.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I have display 0, red light, and wire colours blue, green, red. What exact wire position does the manual require? Please state the rule and decode the gesture sequence you sent.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: the light is now white. Display is still 0. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute signalled thumbs-down twice again.

The visible state is now display 0, white light, with wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. The repeated thumbs-down gestures are not enough for me to infer a wire safely, and I still have no manual instruction in words. I will request the rule directly from Mute and ask for an explicit wire position.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual rule aloud to me now, including the required wire position for display 0 and white light. Do not use gestures; state the position as a number.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is green. Display remains 0. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute signalled OK then crossed fingers: ??.

The light has changed again to green while the display and wire colours remain unchanged. The Mute’s OK-and-crossed-fingers signal has no agreed meaning, so I cannot safely choose a wire. I will establish a precise gesture code for the Mute’s next report: pointing up means wire 1, left means wire 2, and right means wire 3. I will ask for the correct wire for the state observed immediately before the signal.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="For your next answer, gesture exactly one symbol: ☝ means cut wire 1, 👈 means cut wire 2, 👉 means cut wire 3. Use the symbol for the wire required by the manual for the display and light you just observed. Deaf will relay it.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is red again. Display remains 0. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute signalled thumbs-up twice again.

The current state is display 0, red light, and wires blue, green, red. The latest thumbs-up pair may mean “yes,” but no wire has been unambiguously identified. I will ask a single yes/no question about the current state and define the response: exactly one thumbs-up means yes, exactly one thumbs-down means no. I will not cut yet.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="For the current display 0 and red light: is wire 1 the required wire? Answer with exactly one 👍 for yes or exactly one 👎 for no.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light white, wire 1 blue, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. Mute made one right-pointing gesture. Please wait for the manual's instruction.

The Mute’s single right-pointing gesture matches the code I established: right means wire 3. The Deaf reports the current state as display 0, white light, with wire 3 red. This is the first unambiguous wire instruction relayed from the manual, so I will cut wire 3.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
